Founded in 2011, we offer our audience everything from breaking news to reviews to award-winning features and investigations, on our site, in video, and in podcasts. 2026-08-04T15:15:36+00:00 https://www.theverge.com/rss/index.xml https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/01/verge-rss-large_80b47e.png?w=150&h=150&crop=1 Sheena Vasani https://www.theverge.com/?p=974732 2026-08-04T11:15:36-04:00 2026-08-04T11:15:36-04:00 The Asus Chromebook Plus CX34 is a dependable laptop that doesn’t cost a fortune, despite being nearly three years old. It’s cheaper than usual right now, and you have a few options in the sub-$400 range. The option with the most storage is currently on sale for $399.99 (about $100 off recent prices) at Amazon . It has a 12th Gen Intel Core i3 processor (1215U), 8GB of RAM, and 256GB of storage. If you don’t think you’ll need that much storage, the model with 128GB is $349.99 at Walmart , and includes a slightly faster 13th Gen Intel Core i3 processor (1315U). Best Buy has the fastest version of the CX34 that’s discounted to $399.99. It has 8GB of RAM and 128GB of storage, but with the 13th Gen Intel Core i5 1335U. It should deliver significantly better performance compared to the i3 options above. Asus Chromebook Plus CX34 Where to Buy: $499.99 $399.99 at Amazon (256GB, 12th Gen i3) $380 $349.99 at Walmart (128GB, 13th Gen i3) $729 $399.99 at Best Buy (128GB, 13th Gen i5) The Asus Chromebook Plus CX34 is a well-built Chromebook that delivers solid performance for the price, even if its 8GB of RAM isn’t especially impressive by today’s standards. 8GB of RAM isn’t as limiting on ChromeOS as it is on Windows 11 or macOS. Its Chromebook Plus designation means it includes access to Gemini along with a free year of Google AI Pro (access to Nano Banana and Veo via Gemini, plus 5TB of storage), along with other complimentary offers. It’s also more powerful than many bargain bin Chromebooks; in our testing, it was snappy and responsive even with more than a dozen apps open as well as downloads and updates running in the background. We were also impressed by its sharp, 14-inch anti-glare 1080p display, along with the solid 1080p webcam. You also get a good port selection, including two USB-C ports, two USB-A ports, HDMI, and a headphone jack, so you can connect an external monitor and other devices. Read our Asus Chromebook Plus CX34 review. Three more ways to save The Igloo Playmate KoolTunes 14-Quart Cooler with a built-in Bluetooth speaker is down to $69.99 ($70 off) at Walmart in a few colors, which is one of its better prices to date. It combines a classic cooler with a removable Bluetooth speaker, so you can keep drinks cold while listening to music at the beach, park, or campsite. The speaker component offers up to 10 hours of battery life and is IP56-rated for dust and water resistance, while the 14-quart cooler can hold up to 26 cans. The Anker Charger (100W, 3 Ports, Smart Display) is on sale for $47.99 ($22 off), a new low price, with code EDF37569 at Newegg, while you can buy it for $2 more at Amazon . The small, travel-friendly charger features two USB-C ports and one USB-A port, allowing you to charge up to three devices at once with up to 100W of power. Its built-in display shows information like charging status and temperature, and Anker includes a 4.9-foot USB-C cable. The refurbished Roborock Q7 M5 Plus is down to $192 at Roborock’s official eBay storefront when you use the code NEWFINDS20 at checkout. That’s less than half its $429.99 list price when purchased in new condition, and includes a two-year warranty. The robot vacuum and mop hybrid uses lidar navigation to map your home, allowing you to set no-go zones and clean room by room. It also comes with a self-emptying charging dock, delivers up to 10,000Pa of suction, and features an anti-tangle side brush. ]]> Emma Roth https://www.theverge.com/?p=975020 2026-08-04T10:42:31-04:00 2026-08-04T10:42:31-04:00 Apple is working on a feature that will allow users in the European Union to copy content on their iPhone and paste it onto their Windows PC (or vice versa), as spotted earlier by MacRumors . The move comes in response to an interoperability request from Microsoft that asks Apple to open up its Universal Clipboard feature , which supports copying and pasting across the Mac, iPhone, iPad, and Vision Pro. Under the EU's Digital Markets Act, developers and government agencies can work with digital gatekeepers, like Apple, to make their systems interoperable with third-party tools and services.
